judgements.justification: Both area chairs followed their reviewers; A's meta-review adds a formal-proof request but sets no tier above or below the 7-8 scores.
Neither committee rested its spotlight on a forecast of impact beyond the paper's setting; both cite the first lower bound and the separation from mixtures.
The authors' prior-work reply moved A's Reviewer_A5qv up to 7, while no B score moved; this only narrowed A's spread and changed no tier.
Each committee holds one thin 8 (A's 8XsW, B's LQDD) beside substantive reviews, so neither committee's scrutiny is thinner than the other's.
Issues raised by one committee only (A5qv's conceptual gain, twpW's list aspect, iqKa's reference variance) lowered no final score or tier.
Both committees weighed the shared SoS-versus-SQ caveat and the DKS17/DKS19 reliance the same way, as framing and a non-trivial adaptation.
No score changed after reviewer discussion; A5qv's raise followed the authors' response.
No rating clearly disagrees with its own text; iqKa's 7 with 'a great paper' sits within the accept range.
No reviewer gave a borderline score; the least sure reviewers (A's 9D9p, B's NeJG) still rated 8 and 7.
Neither committee had an outlying reviewer, and neither area chair adopted one reviewer's verdict.
Similar verdicts sit at similar scores (A 7, 8, 8, 8; B 7, 7, 8, 8), and the recommendations agree.
Both committees had reviewers above the accept level (8s) and reached the same tier; agreement was not read as grounds for a higher tier than the other committee.
A5qv rose on a checkable argument about prior work (DKS19 needs an unknown covariance), not on new unchecked results or promised revisions.

B's three-sentence meta-review drops iqKa's SoS caveat (only quotation marks around 'matches' remain), while A's meta-review carries 9Tob's caveat forward as a formal-proof request; the tier did not change.
No wrong claim about the paper's own results fed a score; LQDD's 'information-theoretic' label marks a thin review, not the basis of the 8.
The authors conceded the SoS gap to both committees in the same words, and both treated it as framing, so it lifted neither committee above the other.
No objection or score change came after the response period.
Both area chairs reached the same tier from near-identical scores.
Both area chairs' recommendations match their best-informed reviewers (A's 9Tob and 9D9p, B's twpW and iqKa).
Neither committee had concerns that the rebuttal could not answer; the shared SoS caveat got the same reply in both.
No outlying score; all eight ratings are 7 or 8.
No outlying reviewer.
Neither committee had a detractor to set aside; both were weighed for and given a spotlight.
Neither committee raised audience breadth or venue fit.
A's meta-review cites a reviewer discussion not in the visible record, but it states the reviewers' positions and the rebuttal's effect correctly; B's states nothing wrong.
A's 8s never replied, but the response answered no point that bore on their scores; B's reviewers all acknowledged it, and no score in B moved either.
Each committee has one reviewer who did not check the proofs (A's 9D9p, B's NeJG), and the substantive reviews alone are still all-accept in both.
Neither committee was split.
The authors sent both committees the same text on the shared SoS caveat.

A's Reviewer_A5qv first judged the conceptual gain limited because a d^2 bound 'follows from DKS17'; the paper credits that bound to DKS19, which needs an unknown covariance and does not transfer. The error held A5qv's first score down until the rebuttal corrected it.
Neither meta-review justifies spotlight over poster, but both committees reached the same tier from similar scores, so no tier rises above the other's support.
No reviewer contested the paper's framing from a neighbouring field's premises.
Both committees had engaged reviewers at 8 (A's 9D9p, B's twpW), and neither had critics to argue against.
No committee judged promised fixes too large for camera-ready.
A's meta-review mentions a reviewer discussion not in the record, but it settled no split; the scores were unanimous accept.
Both committees judged the theory paper on the same terms.
No below-threshold score was held.

reasoning: Both committees recommended a spotlight from all-accept scores (A 7, 8, 8, 8; B 7, 7, 8, 8), saw the same strengths and the same SoS-versus-SQ caveat, and got the same reply to it, so I judged only the small divergences in how each record reached the tier. Three existing reasons name mechanisms present here: A5qv's first score in A rested on a wrong account of prior work (R30), the authors' reply corrected it and moved A5qv while no B score moved (R03), and B's meta-review dropped its reviewer's caveat while A's carried it forward (R14). None of these changed a tier. The thin 8 in each slate and the missing spotlight rationale in both meta-reviews are symmetric, so the reasons that need one committee to differ do not apply. No cause outside the existing set appears, so I added no reason.
